claims.text: Introducing a dual-phase lamellar microstructure can improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy has a single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
The proposed lamellar microstructure combines a soft FCC phase with a hard BCC phase.
A dual-phase structure enables a combination of high strength and high ductility.
Strain-induced martensitic transformation mediates the strength-ductility improvement in the proposed FCC/BCC lamellar eutectic alloy.
Deformation nano-twinning mediates the strength-ductility improvement.
The proposed microstructure will improve both tensile strength and tensile ductility relative to a single-phase solid-solution baseline.
Avoiding brittle intermetallic compounds is necessary for the intervention to succeed.
Maintaining high configurational entropy is necessary for the intervention to succeed.
The optimal FCC/BCC combination and phase proportions are unknown.
Failure of the dual-phase lamellar specimens to improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The task specifies an unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, but the hypothesis instead defines a single-phase solid-solution baseline and proposes introducing the lamellar structure itself. It therefore does not address an intervention applied to the requested existing lamellar-colony state.
